title: test(console): StudioRoute.metadataArea-28561 and AppContent.aiChatEntryGate-37833 read the route probe before its push effect flushes, and red Test UI shards on PRs that don't touch them
body:
repo:objectstack#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibyUSf2nKJWW6qBemSU

## Why this matters

`Test UI` is a required check. Two route tests in `@object-ui/console` fail on slow runners on PRs that mount none of their code. Each failure costs the PR a re-run, and when the re-run fails as well, the PR waits for a test fix it has nothing to do with. This is the same pattern as #37972 (an assertion that reads the first render before the state it pins has settled). There is a third case in two days.

## What fails

- `StudioRoute.metadataArea-28561.test.tsx`, "/studio/~all lands on Setup's environment directory, in one hop, never on a pillar": `expected [ '/studio/~all' ] to deeply equal [ '/studio/~all', …(1) ]`. It went red on PR #37962 (`Test UI (13/16)`, run 46006286439, passed on its one re-run) and again on PR #37970 (`Test UI (13/16)`, run 46013899997, an 877 s shard).
- `AppContent.aiChatEntryGate-37833.test.tsx`, "no AI seat: home is the next entry", new from #37960. It went red on PR #37970 (`Test UI (2/16)`, same run).

L1-c read both on #37970 (comment 7220995813): the DOM already shows the routed target, but the probe's `useEffect` push has not flushed when the assertion reads the history array.

## Acceptance

- Both cases wait for the probe's recorded history to reach its final value (`waitFor` on the array, or the probe records synchronously) before they assert. They do not assert on the first non-empty reading.
- Each keeps its teeth. An ablation that makes the route take two hops, or that lands on a pillar, still reds the Studio case. An ablation that changes the next entry still reds the gate case.
- No other assertion in either file is loosened. If other route-probe tests in `ui/apps/console` share the same probe helper and the same race, the PR names them, and it fixes them only if they use the same helper.
